What Drives Fence Staining Cost

  • Linear footage: the total run of fence is the biggest factor.

  • Wood condition: weathered, graying, or previously coated wood needs more prep.

  • Cleaning & prep: pressure washing and brightening before stain helps it absorb and last.

  • Product choice: transparent, semi-transparent, and solid stains differ in cost and lifespan.

  • One side vs. both sides: staining both faces of the fence increases material and labor.

  • Height and gates: taller panels and gates add detail work.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much does fence staining cost?

Fence staining is priced per linear foot based on the length of your fence, the wood's condition, and the product chosen. Exact per-linear-foot figures are being finalized — book a free estimate for an accurate number for your fence.

How often should I re-stain my fence?

In the Gulf Coast climate, most fences benefit from re-staining every few years; semi-transparent and solid stains last longer than transparent finishes.

Do you stain both sides of the fence?

We can stain one or both visible faces. Staining both sides increases material and labor, which is reflected in the estimate.

Do you clean the fence before staining?

Yes. Cleaning and, where needed, brightening the wood helps the stain absorb evenly and last longer.
